title: AI Regulation and Regulatory Expectations of Boards
summary: The legal and regulatory obligations AI creates for the firm and the board: how jurisdictions are regulating AI, how this overlays existing financial services rules, and what supervisors and auditors expect to see.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The legal and regulatory obligations AI creates for the firm and the board: how jurisdictions are regulating AI, how this overlays existing financial services rules, and what supervisors and auditors expect to see.
Learning Objectives: Explain the main approaches to AI regulation and the duties they place on firms
Identify which of the firm's AI uses are likely to be treated as high-risk and the assurance they require
Prepare the board to evidence oversight to supervisors and auditors
Syllabus: Approaches to AI regulation across jurisdictions: risk-based laws, sectoral rules, supervisory guidance and managing divergence
International standards and frameworks, including OECD, NIST, ISO/IEC 42001, IOSCO, FSB and BIS
Interaction with existing conduct, prudential, consumer protection and data protection rules
Preparing for supervisory engagement: what the board should be able to show
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk, audit and technology committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for AI, risk and compliance
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No technical background in AI or data science is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)
